notes:
A CORRECTION, NOT A NEW ADJUDICATION. 60 rows carried a TP verdict keyed at a caller's positional call argument. aurora_lint 1418 relocated EXP34-C's report off the caller line (Brandon's ruling of 2026-09-21: the dereference is the violation site, a positional argument at a call is not), so a TP keyed at such a line places the verdict at a site the standard no longer treats as one. Each row is corrected AS KEYED and carries no claim about any other site.

HOW THE SET WAS DRAWN. 6,031 labeled EXP34-C keys no longer produce a report at aurora_lint ca327445 over the same codebase_commit (5,934 FP, 69 TP, 21 uncertain, 7 FN). Only the TP rows are in scope -- a stale FP or uncertain key costs nothing to leave. Each of the 69 was classified by the report it actually carried in a run over the same codebase_commit, not by reading the source line alone, because a line can hold both a call and a dereference and only the report says which one the rule keyed:
  - 60 carried a positional-argument call-site report naming the argument and the callee. 59 of them reported at the run 270 baseline (aurora_lint 2960cd88); the 60th, raylib src/rcore.c:2297, was already silent at 270 and was classified from run 268, the last run in which it reported (raylib is pinned at the same codebase_commit across runs 244-270). All 60 are corrected here.
  - 9 are HELD, listed below. None is corrected, and this batch takes no position on any of them.

THE 9 HELD ROWS, AND WHY EACH IS OUT OF REACH OF THIS BASIS.
  (a) 1 whose argument sits in a variadic slot: hostap src/drivers/driver_nl80211_event.c:3579 (wpa_msg is PRINTF_FORMAT(3,4)). 1418 KEPT the call-site check for vararg slots, so that key is still a violation site under the new standard. Correcting it would assert the opposite of what the standard says; its silence is a coverage question, not staleness.
  (b) 8 that carried a dereference report, never a positional-argument one, and stopped reporting well before the relocation (last reporting run between 127 and 238, against a 270 baseline), so 1418 is not their cause. A dereference is the site the new standard treats as THE violation site, so the relocation rationale does not reach them in either direction; they need adjudication on their merits. They are: hostap src/common/wpa_common.c:1277, src/common/wpa_ctrl.c:470 and :726, wpa_supplicant/p2p_supplicant.c:4350 and :4375; mosquitto src/websockets.c:147; raylib src/raudio.c:1707 and src/rmodels.c:2902.

NOT IN SCOPE, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT LOST. The 7 stale FN rows are a separate problem: an FN key that no longer fires is not stale in the TP/FP sense, because the rule still does not report the construct. Untouched here; they need their own pass.

Which commit silenced a given key does not change this correction -- the standard is about the site, not about the commit -- so no per-commit A/B was run. Attributing a key to 1418 specifically would need 4bbf15d1^ vs 4bbf15d1. No EXP34-C precision or recall claim follows from this batch.

Applied on dev-180 under bmdb 1423, corpus-check clean on all 12 pins.
